LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Sole possession of first place in the NFC North is on the line at Ford Field as two 8-2 rivals clash on Thanksgiving with long winning streaks Imagn Images In the first of three Thanksgiving day games, the Detroit Lions play host to the division rival Chicago Bears in one of the biggest games of the NFL season to date. Detroit enters this game winners of six straight and sitting in first place in the NFC North with an 8-2 record. The Lions sport one of the NFL's most efficient and explosive offenses, and their efense hasn't allowed more than 21 points in a game since all the way back in Week 4. The Lions are dealing with injury issues on that side of the ball, but they've held up surprisingly well. That will be put to the test on Thursday afternoon. Chicago comes into this game having won five in a row and sporting an 8-2 record that matches that of Detroit, with the Bears sitting in second place in the division by virtue of a tiebreaker. The Bears also have one of the league's best offenses, while the defense has been strengthened by the acquisition of superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons , who seems to have transformed the unit up front and allowed everything else to click properly into place. That unit, too, will be tested more than ever here. Which of these two teams will keep its winning streak alive and lay claim to sole possession of first place in the division? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Lions vs. Bears live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location: Ford Field (Detroit) TV: CBS | Streaming: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -2.5, O/U 55.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago is eighth in total yards and eighth in total points this season, but some of that has to do with volume. The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Some of that is due to the fact that Caleb Williams missed several games with a hamstring injury, but even with Williams on the field the Bears' EPA per play mark is only the equivalent of the 10th-best offense in the league. Chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai , who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games. The Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year. Chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers , for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap. Still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air. Detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as big a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond . When the Lions have the ball The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run. Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating. He's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns. St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target. Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target. The Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon. That's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line. Detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but he's generally given adequate time to throw. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Welcome to the most special week in the NFL . We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day." Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories. Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Chicago Bears (-1.5) at Detroit Lions (Thursday) Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28 Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30 Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (Thursday) Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans , but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers , and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971… Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20 Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24 Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (-3) (Thursday) Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III . I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16 Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17 Denver Broncos (-3.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers (Friday) Dajani ( Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end … Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13 Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph . I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10 Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7) Dajani ( Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18 Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense. … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20 Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3) Dajani ( 49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season. Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20 Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) (SNF) Dajani ( Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza

The Lions are coming off a 31-21 defeat of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11. Meanwhile, Chicago prevailed against the New Orleans Saints last week, 21-13. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 12 matchup with Chicago. Christian Booher The Lions and Bears are meeting in what is the biggest Thanksgiving in recent memory for the franchise. The team that wins this game will step into the driver's seat for the NFC North with six games remaining and could put themselves in position to contend for the No. 1 seed. As a result, I'm predicting that Dan Campbell will try to bring the fight to the Bears and be ultra-aggressive. With how explosive the Bears' offense can be, I expect Campbell to press the issue and go for it on multiple fourth-downs. This could turn into a shootout, but I think the Lions' ability to run the ball and manage the clock will be the difference-maker. After years of struggles on Thanksgiving, the Lions get over the hump and defeat the Bears in a barnburner. Lions 33, Bears 28 If the Lions are going to notch their seventh straight victory Thursday, they're going to have to absolutely earn it. They're set to face one of their stiffest tests of the season, going up against Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears. Heading into the Week 12 affair, the Bears own both a top-10 offense and a top-10 defense. And just like the Lions, they can absolutely pound the rock. So, I believe this clash between NFC North rivals will come down to who wins the battle in the trenches. While it won't be easy, I believe that Detroit will open up just enough holes for Jahmyr Gibbs to run through, enabling Dan Campbell's squad to secure the Thanksgiving Day victory. Lions 24, Bears 20 John Maakaron The Lions now face their toughest test of the 2026 season. Ben Johnson will have the Bears offense ready to take advantage of certain weaknesses in the Lions’ secondary. While both teams will look to establish the run, Detroit’s offense will execute more consistently. Caleb Williams is turning the football over too much and Kelvin Sheppard’s defense will capitalize. This game could become very high scoring, which favors Detroit. Lions 27, Bears 24 Emmett Matasovsky Thursday is a major test for the Lions, going up against Ben Johnson and the red-hot Chicago Bears. Additionally, this is the Lions’ third game in 11 days, including an overseas flight to Munich, Germany. The Lions have the opportunity to prove that the defensive improvement is more than just a lack of competition. In recent weeks, the Lions have seen their defense shut down the passing game, but their best competition in those contests was against an already injured Baker Mayfield. The Bears have a knack for explosive plays, but also do not grade out well in play action. With Jahmyr Gibbs as the bellcow back in Detroit, that is a mismatch offensive coordinator Drew Petzing can exploit. That said, with the recent injuries to Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell and now underrated pass-rushing defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard, I see the Lions unable to come out on top on Thanksgiving. With the Bears and Lions both sitting at 8-2, there is little room for defensive mistakes in a game that will determine sole possession of first place in the NFC North. Gordon's absence creates another opportunity for rookie Malik Muhammad II, who is listed behind him on the Bears' depth chart. The fourth-round pick out of Texas has already demonstrated that he can handle meaningful responsibilities in Chicago's secondary, including work in the nickel position. The Chicago Bears have a significant challenge waiting for them in Detroit on Thanksgiving, and it has nothing to do with the usual questions surrounding Caleb Williams or Jeffery Simmons. The Bears secondary injuries could force several less-heralded defenders into bigger roles against one of the NFL's most dangerous passing offenses. Malik Muhammad Could Be Asked to Fill Gordon's Role Muhammad made an encouraging NFL debut against Carolina, starting at nickel and playing 76% of the defensive snaps. He also intercepted a pass, helping Chicago preserve its lead in the eventual victory. That experience could become particularly valuable against Detroit, where Muhammad may have to handle an increased workload against a receiving group featuring Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Bears' official depth chart makes him the natural candidate to absorb some of Gordon's responsibilities. Clark Phillips III Has Another Chance to Build on Breakout Performance If Stevenson cannot play, Clark Phillips III could become even more important. Listed as Stevenson's backup, Phillips has already given Chicago a reason to trust him after delivering one of his best performances in a Bears uniform against New Orleans. Phillips forced a fumble, recorded his first NFL sack and earned one of three defensive game balls from head coach Ben Johnson in Sunday's 21-13 victory. He also finished with four tackles and a pass defended. Acquired from Atlanta in the August trade that sent defensive tackle Gervon Dexter to the Falcons, Phillips is beginning to demonstrate why Chicago wanted him. Another strong performance against Detroit would strengthen his case for a more permanent role, particularly with Gordon still sidelined and Stevenson's availability uncertain. The Lions did not want to throw too much at Joseph, so they had no issue with him being a third defensive back behind Clark and Brian Branch. However, Joseph would have pushed Clark into a reserve role at some point anyway. Now, Detroit might have to start Joseph in Week 12. If that is the case, they are unlikely to look back. Still, the Lions will continue to use their three-safety looks. Brian Branch moves into the slot in nickel looks. The difference would be that Clark would only play on nickel snaps, which is what Joseph did in his debut. Right now, Clark might not play at all. Christian Izien or Keith Abney would assume the nickel safety role. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Thanksgiving clash between NFC East rivals Kathryn Riley / Getty Images FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games. The only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day. After Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10. "It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak." Quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford currently share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each. "It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott said Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted." However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year. "It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," said Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving." That's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve. "Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb . "I hope he don't go crazy." Let's dig into the matchup. Where to watch Cowboys vs. Eagles live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Location: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas) TV: FOX | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -8.5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Prescott is cooking right now. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season. Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10. "It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier." In their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year. Cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status was uncertain because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report after he practiced fully on Wednesday, indicating he will indeed play. When the Eagles have the ball When the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley . Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style. Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving , who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams said the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going. Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter . Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars ' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research . He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott said he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage. "Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams said. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices." The present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. He'll break the tie with Brady with his 21st such victory in a row on Thanksgiving. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights One bold prediction for each of the NFL rivalry showcases on Thanksgiving Imagn Images The most American way to celebrate Thanksgiving is spending time with family, going back and forth from the table or couch with multiple plates of food and watching all three games of NFL football. Thursday's course will be the first Thanksgiving game in league history between two teams on winning streaks of five or more games when the NFC North rival Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Detroit Lions (8-2) square off. The league's midday entree will feature two of the biggest brands in football -- the Philadelphia and the Dallas Cowboys . A fun day of football will then be wrapped up with an AFC rivalry showdown between Patrick Mahomes ' Kansas City Chiefs and Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills . What stunning events could occur in each of the three games? Here's one bold prediction for all three courses on the Thanksgiving menu. Lions intercept Caleb Williams three times The Detroit Lions are going to intercept Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams three times in Detroit on Thanksgiving. Yes, the Lions defense was a league laughingstock through the first five weeks of the season, ranking last in the NFL in both total yards allowed per game (404.4) and passing yards allowed per game (297.4). However, they have been a top-five unit in scoring defense (14.4 points per game allowed, fourth in the NFL), total defense (248.6 total yards per game, third in the NFL) and pass defense (168.6 passing yards per game allowed) since Pro Bowl defensive back Brian Branch's return from a torn Achilles after the team's Week 6 bye. In Week 11, Detroit saw All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph return from his lingering knee injury, which made Sunday the first time he and Branch have played together this season. When Branch and Joseph played in 29 of a possible 34 games together from 2023 to 2024, they combined for 20 interceptions, the most by any teammate duo in the league in that span. Their renewed partnership in the Lions secondary will lead to Williams tossing three interceptions on Thanksgiving. Prescott will do so for a third time and his second against the Eagles on Thanksgiving. Prescott is on fire at the moment. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and 5-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25) while ranking eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season. With Eagles All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) hampered by injury and uncertain to suit up on Thursday, Prescott and Pro Bowl wide receivers CeeDee Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) go nuclear on the fading 3-7 Eagles. Chiefs and Bills combine for under 45 points Mahomes and the Chiefs (8-2) versus Allen and the Bills (9-1) is the best quarterback rivalry today. Thanksgiving will be their 11th matchup, with each side having five wins. Mahomes' Chiefs are 4-0 in the playoffs, while Allen's Bills are 5-1 in the regular season, with Buffalo winning the last five regular-season matchups. This game on Turkey Day will be just the second game in NFL history with both teams fresh off of at least three consecutive wins of three scores, along with Tom Brady's New England Patriots (8-0) versus Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts (7-0) in 2007, per CBS Sports Research. However, their blowout have come against suspect competition. Buffalo has won four in a row by 17-plus points while facing six backup quarterbacks in this stretch, and Kansas City has won three in a row by 21-plus points against the sagging New York Jets (3-8), Atlanta Falcons (3-7) and Arizona Cardinals (3-8). Entering Week 12, Mahomes co-leads the league in touchdown-to-interception (5.5, 22-4) along with C.J. Stroud , and Allen's 25 total touchdowns (14 passing and 11 rushing) are the third most in the league this season. However, scoring against each other instead of teams in disarray will be a lot more difficult, with the Chiefs having the NFL's No. 2 scoring defense (16.3 points per game allowed) and the Bills having the NFL's No. 9 scoring defense (20.8 points per game allowed. That will lead to both sides combining to score under 45 points, meaning this matchup of Mahomes vs. Allen won't be any more high-scoring than 24-20. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Legendary quarterbacks close out the holiday slate in one of the biggest games of the season Getty Images The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs . A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date. As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye. This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons. Both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's New England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts . The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one. Where to watch Bills vs. Chiefs live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, N.Y.) TV: NBC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Bills vs. Chiefs key storylines Another Allen vs. Mahomes classic: A pair of all-time great quarterbacks have quite the history in head-to-head battles at this stage of their careers, and there is a sharp dichotomy between their records in regular-season matchups and playoff battles. While Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in the regular season, Mahomes has been dominant in win-or-go-home situations at 4-0. In games against each other, their passing numbers are nearly identical; Allen passed for 1,534 yards and 11 touchdowns to Mahomes' 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns in their first 10 clashes. Where Allen owns a decided edge is in ball security (three interceptions vs. eight) and in rushing production (five touchdowns vs. zero). Top-tier running back showdown: Messaging out of Kansas City is that the Chiefs are hopeful Kenneth Walker III will return to action on Thursday following a two-game absence due to groin tightness. If he suits up, then the NFL is in for a tremendous running back battle. Walker (109.0) and Buffalo's James Cook III (106.0) rank second and third, respectively, in rushing yards per game and are in a race with Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs for the league rushing title. If Cook can return to the top of the leaderboard, he would pace the NFL in yardage for the second consecutive year. On Sunday, he set a new record for the most consecutive games (nine) with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a season. Bills defense levels up: Over the first six games of the season, the Bills had to post gaudy scoring numbers in order to make up for a leaky defense. That was not the case in any of their last four games. All of a sudden, this unit ranks 11th in EPA per play allowed, has not surrendered more than 12 points in a game since Oct. 18 and is no longer a liability but rather an asset. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit has gone 15 quarters without allowing a touchdown, which is the NFL's longest single-season streak since 2000. The group still has to prove that it can play at this level against more formidable competition, though. Chiefs ride historic hot streak: Just like their upcoming opponent, the Chiefs enjoyed a stretch of games against lesser competition heading into the Thanksgiving battle and took care of business with ease. In routs of the New York Jets , Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals , the Chiefs tied the longest streak in franchise history of wins by at least 21 points (three). Even dating back to their last loss, Mahomes is in the midst of a scalding stretch with 13 passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Bills vs. Chiefs prediction It is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and shows all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into. At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day." Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories. Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Chicago Bears (-1.5) at Detroit Lions (Thursday) Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28 Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30 Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (Thursday) Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans , but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers , and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III . In a classic tilt between all-world quarterbacks, dynamic head coaches and elite rushing attacks, many are calling for bushels of points on Thursday. On the other hand, an ugly weather report for the holiday may have different plans. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 12 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: This has been true for a large number of Chiefs-Bills matchups in the past, but this game truly feels like a coin-flip. The loss of Kenneth Walker matters, but the Bills have unanswered questions on both sides of the ball. Buffalo wins these regular-season showdowns, but it’s arguably more important for Kansas City this time through. The Chiefs’ offensive tackles are cause for concern, but Patrick Mahomes has been playing tremendous football behind that same line for much of this season. James Cook is a weapon, but Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is typically stout against the run. Ultimately, this feels like a game that comes down to a late field goal or a fourth-quarter turnover. I’m relatively confident that this game will live up to the hype, but I could easily see either team escaping with the narrow victory. Jordan Foote: In my Week 12 preview, I echoed Brisco's sentiment and chalked this one up to a relative coin-flip as well. The Bills have plenty of holes on their roster and, in many ways, remind me of this Chiefs squad. Usually, having home-field advantage would be the deciding factor in a game like this, but Buffalo simply doesn't look like a club that's firing on all cylinders. The Kansas City defense will surely be put to the test against the dynamic rushing duo of Allen and Cook. There also may not be a more lethal play extender than Allen in the dropback game when he's operating at peak capacity. Still, the Chiefs have a running game of their own with Johnson enjoying some success. A heavy ball-control style of outing goes to KC. Expect a close one at the new Highmark Stadium. I'm not rolling with a combined 60-plus points, instead giving the visitors a one-score edge thanks to either a timely stop on defense or some Mahomes magic on the other side of the football. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are looking to change their fortunes against the Bills in the regular season. Patrick Mahomes may own Josh Allen in the postseason, but he’s 1-5 against Buffalo in regular-season meetings. With Kenneth Walker out for the third consecutive week, Emmett Johnson will take on a larger workload in his place. He’ll need to have a big day with cold temperatures and heavy rainfall expected in Buffalo. While the Chiefs have bounced back in a huge way since their two-game losing skid, they haven’t faced much competition. Behind Buffalo’s defense improved defense and a rowdy home crowd, I think it’ll be tough for the Chiefs to pull this one off. Tyler Brown: This is the kind of game that comes down to the last possession, and I think it ends up going Kansas City’s way despite Mahomes’ 1-5 record against Allen in the regular season. I think they match up that well. Allen is playing somewhat erratically, as shown by his nine touchdowns and nine interceptions over the past eight games. The Bills’ defense has looked great against backup quarterbacks, but it allows more than 30 points a game against good-to-average offenses, and Kansas City is as good as any. Mahomes has been dealing for a month, and he should find openings against a vulnerable defensive backfield. With Emmett Johnson carrying the load, the rushing attack will keep the Bills guessing. Travis Kelce, Josh Downs, and Rashee Rice can do the rest. It will not be easy to stop Allen, and you have to account for Cook as well. Allen always seems to find another gear against this team, and the Chiefs will have to keep him out of the red zone, where he is a touchdown vulture. But in a possible Thanksgiving shootout in the rain, I like the team that appears more balanced. The Chiefs have only one win against a team with a winning record, so this could be fool’s gold, but the process behind their recent surge looks legitimate. He's feeling pretty good, though.” KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related The Chiefs placed FB Ben VanSumeren on injured reserve , so he won't appear on the injury report for the remainder of the week. He must miss at least four games while on IR. Coach Reid described his injury as a knee sprain, so he could realistically return this season. Chiefs RG Trey Smith fully participated in practice. Coach Reid suggested that he's on track to return for Week 12. Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott remains limited in practice as he recovers from his ACL injury. I think it'll likely be at least another week before he returns to action. They only had a walkthrough, but four players saw their status upgraded for the Bills on Tuesday.
